rejected_claims.title: Abstract type named in [MessagePackFormatter]/[MessagePackKnownFormatter] is now silently ignored
rejected_claims.claim: TryCreate is not only used for discovery: it also resolves the type in a member's [MessagePackFormatter(typeof(X))] (TypeCollector.GetSpecialFormatter) and in [MessagePackKnownFormatter(typeof(X))]. For an abstract X these now return 'not a formatter', and the else branch that should report it is commented out, so a user who points an attribute at an abstract formatter gets no diagnostic (on base the KnownFormatter path would have produced MsgPack013 for the missing instance) and the generator falls back to treating the member as if it had no custom formatter. Nothing in the diff tests these paths; I did not run them, so the exact downstream diagnostics/codegen are unverified.
